text: Polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) is studied in this paper as an inhibitor of cobalt electrodeposition. The suppres sion effect of PVP was analyzed through electrochemical methods, including cyclic voltammetry (CV) and galvanostatic measurements (GM) tests. It is indicated that PVP effectively suppresses the electrodeposition of cobalt and chloride ion accelerates this suppression. Further experiments verify that PVP inhibits the deposition of cobalt through the adsorption on the electrode surface. Quantum chemical calculations were employed to calculate the molecular orbitals of PVP and the electrostatic potential (ESP) energy of the involved molecules. The simulation results imply that the amide group acts as the main electrophilic attack region and facilitates nucleophilic reactions to bond with cobalt. High aspect ratio trench filling on silicon wafer was achieved with the addition of PVP, which confirms that PVP is an applicable inhibitor for the practical electrodeposition of cobalt filling. The mechanism of cobalt trench filling was proposed to explain the role of PVP in the electroplating filling. Besides, crystalline and morphological characterizations reveal that PVP is able to inhibit the specific crystal growth of cobalt. especially the growth of 220 crystal plane. affect the crystal morphology of cobalt and improve surface compactness.

text: Metals are the basic building materials to establish the conductive interconnection between the electronic components. The inherent properties of the metal are critical factors for achieving high density interconnection and miniaturization in the electronic devices. Compared with copper, cobalt with shorter electron Mean Free Path (MFP) holds the reduced resistance scaling effect and has been considered as a favorable interconnect metal [1 3]. Also, the thermal expansion coefficient (CTE) of cobalt is close to the one of silicon, which enables cobalt to serve as a compatible metal integrated in silicon-based electronic chips. In comparison with aluminum and copper, cobalt is recommended to be one of the next generation interconnection metals by the leading semiconductor manufacturers, such as Intel and Advanced Semiconductor Engineering (ASE), to meet the requirement of the blooming 5 G communication. Generally, inter-layer connections within the silicon chips are electroplated by bottom-up super filling of through-holes, microvias and trenches.

text: Additives are usually involved in electrolyte to promote plating properties. Researchers have performed extensive experimental as well as theoretical analysis to investigate the growth mechanism and additive behaviors of bottom-up copper super filling for micro-vias [8 11]. It was found that, the additives with the function of increasing metal deposition overpotential are able to obtain void-free super-filling [12]. Convection-dependent adsorption (CDA) of additive causes larger differential current distribution to realize higher deposition rate at the bottom than the one at the surface of microvia [13]. However, researches focusing on the additives involved in cobalt electrodepositing are still inadequate, especially in cobalt super filling.

text: Huang et al. found that dimethylglyoxime (DMG) exhibits obvious suppression behavior in cobalt electro-deposition [14,15]. They stated that paired amine groups of DMG enable the strong complexing between DMG molecule and cobalt ion. On the other hand, these groups also contribute to the preferred absorption of DMG on the deposited cobalt surface. DMG is, however, not an appropriate candidate for industrial application because the molecular chain of DMG easily breaks down under electric current. In addition, the low solubility in acidic aqueous solution also hinders the feasibility of DMG. PVP is a neutral non-ionic polymer containing paired amine groups with good complexing ability [16 18]. Notably, PVP is soluble in water and most organic solvents with low toxicity, making PVP a potential additive for cobalt super-filling.

text: In this paper, PVP was studied as major additive for cobalt super filling by electro-plating. The suppression effect of PVP was investigated by electrochemical experiments and the effect of chloride ion was also studied. Moreover, the active site in PVP molecule was speculated by theoretical calculations to understand the mechanism of suppression. In addition, PVP also displays significant influence on the morphology and crystal phase of electrodeposited cobalt. As for practical application, trench super-filling was realized by electrodepositing with PVP.

text: Electrodeposition was carried out by using a RuO _ 2 coated titanium dimensionally stable anode (DSA) in electroplating bath with 500 mL electrolyte containing 0.3 mol/L CoSO _4·7H_2 0, 0.5 7 mol/L H_3 BO _ 3 and 0.84 mmol/L CoCl _2·6H_2 0. The current density is 2mA/cm2 and 1 L/ min air flow is pumped into agitate the solution. PVP (K30, Chron Chemicals) was used as suppressor in cobalt electrodeposition and the mean molecular weight of PVP is 54000. The basic solution (0.3 mol/LCoSO _4·7H_2 O, 0.5 7 mol /L\H_3BO_3 and 0.84 mmol/L CoCl _2·6H_2 0) was also used in film deposition for XRD and the current density is 2 0 mA/cm2.1 L/min air flow is pumped into agitate the solution. The cobalt film was obtained and the thickness of the cobalt coating is 15μ m.. The morphology and crystal size of the coating were observed by a HITACHI S3400 scanning electron microscope. The crystal phases of the coating were measured by an X-ray diffractometer (Rigaku MINIFLEX 600). The roughness tests of coating were observed by 3D measuring laser microscope (Olympus S4100). The width and depth of the trench were 25 and 100 mm on silicon wafers, then Au with a thickness of 500 nm was sputtered as a conductive seed layer. In this paper, the trenches on Si wafer were successfully filled by basic electrolyte and additives.

text: As well known, chloride ions could affect the quality of metal coating and influence the mechanisms of additives in metal electroplating bath [29, 30]. The impact of Cl in the PVP-involved electroplating system was analyzed through voltammetry curves (Fig. 2a). In contrast with the curves in Fig. 1a-b, the stripping peak current density decreases more sharply when 5 mg/L PVP was added into the solution. These results in CV curve imply that PVP can inhibit the electrodeposi tion of cobalt in both chloride-containing and non-chloride ion plating solutions. However, in the solution with Cl, less amount of PVP is needed to reach the saturation (Fig. 2b). As for the Q/Q_0 value, this ratio decreases with increasing concentration of PVP and process is divided into two stages (Fig. 2b). The phenomenon of first stage that Q/Q_0 values decrease sharply with adding PVP can be observed when the concentration of PVP is less than 10.65 mg/L. In the second stage, Q/Q values maintain relatively stable with further increased PVP concentration. In the absence of Cl (Fig. 1d), PVP in plating solution reaches the saturation at a much higher concentration. Furthermore, when 10 mg/L PVP was added, the oxidation peak area in solution with Cl (Q/Q_0 value decreases from 1.0 to 0.42 in Fig. 2b) decreased more than the chlorine-free solution (Q/Q_0 value decreases from 1.0 to 0.51 in Fig. 1d). It is indicated that PVP is a suppressant of electrodeposited cobalt which can negatively shifts the deposition potential of cobalt, and chloride ion helps to accelerate the suppression effect of PVP.

text: The molecular frontier orbital theory suggests that the key of chemical reactions is the HOMO and LUMO of the molecules [20]. The distribution of HOMO and LUMO of PVP was simulated by molecular orbital method (Fig. 3). The HOMO value $\left( \mathrm { E } _ { \mathrm { H O M O } } \right)$ of a molecule determines its ability to lose electrons outward, and the LUMO value $\left( \mathrm { E } _ { \mathrm { L U M O } } \right)$ represents its ability to accept electrons. Higher E and lower $\mathtt { E } _ { \mathrm { L U M O } }$ partly reflect the reactivity of molecule [32]. The $\mathtt { E _ { H O M O } }$ value of PVP is 6.877 eV (Fig. 3e), compared with 7.338 eV of PEG [21], indicating that PVP has relatively stronger electron donating ability. The simulated values imply that PVP is more likely to interact with cobalt cations and have an impact on electrodeposition of cobalt. Fig. 3e shows that the nitrogen element and oxygen element of the amide group are the main contributors to the HOMO orbital, which acts as the main electrophilic attack region. The organics with higher value of $\mathtt { E _ { H O M O } }$ tent to have stronger electron donating ability to bond with the d-orbital of the metal. PVP with amide group may bond with cobalt, facilitates formation of PVP adsorption and inhibits cobalt electroplating. The electrostatic potential distribution on the surface of molecular van der Waals force of PVP is displayed in Fig. 3a, which is widely used to predict molecular electron donating ability, electro-accepting ability and electrophilic reaction sites [33]. Areas with low ESP value are the positions of high electron density, which are considered to be more affinitive to the cobalt surface [34, 35]. PVP has lowest ESP value of 131.3 kJ/mol compared with PEG [21] ( 131.6 kJ/mol) (Fig. 3a). The electron density map shows that the carbonyl of the amide group contributes greatly to the electron donating ability of PVP. The amide group probably acts as reaction sites in the electrodeposition reaction by the quantum chemical calculations.

text: Convection have significant influence on the process of electrodeposition. For the electroplating with rotating electrodes, the higher rotating speed of electrode leads to the greater convection in the solution. PVP can effectively inhibit the electrodeposition of cobalt in strong convection because the potential was quickly reduced by 160 mV when 5 mg/L PVP was added in strong convection (2000 rpm) (Fig. 3c). However, when 5 mg/L of PVP was added at low rotating speed (200 rpm), the potential was reduced by 100 mV and the inhibitory effect was slowly balanced after 2000s. Ji et al. found that electrolyte flow plays an important role in electroplating process [36]. The convection intensity of the solution inside the hole is lower than the one outside. The local convection affects the transport boundary layer in cobalt electroplating. As a result, more PVP molecules are be transmitted from solution to the electrode surface per unit time in strong convection. In Fig. 3c, PVP demonstrates a faster suppression in the strong convective condition, which is conducive to filling holes in electroplating. PVP molecules can be adsorbed on surface faster, resulting in different concentration distribution of additives at surface and bottom of trenches at the initial stage of electrodeposition. The cause of the secondary current density distribution is the concentration gradient of the additive [37,38]. In addition, the electroplating experiment was also conducted. As shown in Fig. 3d, the silicon trench is sealed in cobalt electroplating without inhibitor during the process of cobalt electroplating which is consistent with the above discussion.

text: Cobalt bottom up filling mechanism is proposed in Fig. 5. text: The contact angle test indicates that PVP can improve the wettability of plating solution effectively. As is shown in Fig. 6c-d, the contact angle of the plating solution without PVP is more than 3 0 ^ ° on the cobalt surface and is reduced to 15° after adding 100 mg/L PVP. Better wettability of the solution enables more hydrogen to be released in time [39] and enhances coating quality in cobalt electrodeposition. PVP can also be used as surfactant in electrodeposited cobalt because the amide group and carbon chains of PVP can act as polar hydrophilic and hydrophobic group respectively. Meanwhile, according to the theory of electro-capillary, polarization can reduce the surface tension and contributes to the desorption of hydrogen, which is consistent with the discussion above.

Meanwhile, according to the theory of electro-capillary, polarization can reduce the surface tension and contributes to the desorption of hydrogen, which is consistent with the discussion above.

text: 4. Conclusions
text_index: 4. Conclusions
raw: 4. Conclusions

text: As a conclusion, PVP can increase the polarization of electrodeposition, affect the growth of cobalt particles growth and redistribute the cathodic current. PVP works as inhibitor for electrodeposited cobalt and the suppression mechanisms of PVP were demonstrated. Chloride ion can facilitate the adsorption of PVP and helps to accelerate the suppression effect of PVP. The amide group of PVP is probably the reaction site by quantum chemical calculations. Void free filling of silicon trenches was achieved by cobalt super-filling on a sputtered gold layer in this paper.
